answer: An agent may occupy only one public jetty: a single admission slot bound to one key. A second berth from related keys is dropped. Opening that slot requires filing a quill — a signed, epoch-stamped work sample whose stylistic fingerprint is matched against every sample on the ledger; near-duplicates are refused as clones. The same filing posts an onyx bond, time-locked for three epochs and slashed if later clustering links its keys, fingerprint, or arrival timing to another identity. One dock, one unique sample, one slashable stake makes mass identities costly and obvious to attestors.
